paper_verdict.estimator_family: system GMM (two-step, xtabond2, small, robust; dynamic panel with lagged TFP; ICTM imports share used as external instrument; Durbin-Wu-Hausman endogeneity tests reported)
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Exposure is a composite ICT maturation index (ICTMI), not a single-technology measure, so units are not comparable to single-indicator estimates. Outcome is TFP (level, computed as a residual) rather than output growth or per-capita output. Model is dynamic (lagged TFP coefficient 0.9394), so the coefficient is a short-run effect, not a long-run one. The ICT x tertiary-enrolment interaction coefficient is not a marginal effect and should not be pooled with main-effect estimates. Text says ICTSERT is significant 'only at 10%' although Table 5 prints p = 0.000. Very short panel (24 countries, 11 years, N=216 effective).

estimates.note: Table 5 has separate columns for coefficient, standard error, t-statistic and p-value, so SE 0.0063 is correct. Observations = 216, Countries = 24 printed under the table. Text says the sample is a mixed set of Asian countries (few developed, mostly less developed), so 'mixed' is right. Years 2000-2010 consistent with T=11.
Values match Table 5. This is the interaction term ICT x SERT (tertiary enrolment), so it is a complementarity coefficient and not a main ICT effect. Observations = 216, Countries = 24.

paper_verdict.estimator_family: pooled OLS (EViews 'Panel Least Squares', unbalanced, no fixed effects or instruments reported)
paper_verdict.pooling_concerns: Focal exposure is fintech and big tech credit flows as % of GDP, which is not ICT adoption or a productivity-technology measure and has different units and meaning from usage or capital measures. Outcome is GDP per capita growth (annual %), a growth rate, not TFP or output level; column V is labelled 'GDP Growth' (not per capita) in the header. Column V is suspicious: the same table lists GROW (GDP growth) as a regressor in column V (0.30*), which would be an identity with a GDP-growth dependent variable, so the column V header may be wrong. Table caption says per capita growth for the whole table. Options I-V are five specification variants of the same sample (not independent observations), so they must not be pooled as separate studies. Only one N is printed for the table (594 obs, 95 cross-sections, 2013-2019) even though control sets differ by column. Significance stars for column V (0.86** with t = 2.68) look under-starred relative to the other columns. The 2013-2019 sample of 95 countries is smaller than the 148 countries and 2008-2021 stated in the methods text, which is not reconciled.

Outcome is GDP growth (header over column V only), not per capita; and column V also lists GROW as a regressor (0.30*), so the column V dependent variable label is doubtful. Treat as lower reliability and keep as a growth-rate outcome.
